title: Introducing Project Eagle's NEW Engine (100% Billet)

context.location: Proline Racing shop, Georgia (engine pickup + partial top-end assembly by the Cleetus crew under Proline supervision)

caption_corrections.confidence: high (video title context: 'Proline Hemi' in follow-up video title)

people: James, Zach, Sam, George, Jack (Cleetus crew)

base_vehicle.notes: Engine to be installed at Cameron Johnson Race Cars into Eagle

block.notes: dry deck - no water jackets (first engine the crew has had without water jackets); block lightened; lifter bores large/replaceable

heads.notes: roughly twice the size of heads they normally use; heads can be removed without removing intake (slide out from under intake) - designed for between-round service

head_fastening.torque_sequence: 70 ft-lb all, center outward; then upper row 220 ft-lb, lower row 150 ft-lb; repeated 220 checks; some '50 pounders'

pistons.value: billet, big dish to reduce compression for abuse

valvetrain.rockers: shaft rockers, oil fed up through pushrods/adjusters
valvetrain.lash_cold_notes: lash value said as 'six, six' (caption unclear)

intake.brand: Frankenstein (caption) billet intake, braced against backfire
intake.boost_rating: Proline said they have made up to ~80-85 psi through this intake design; baseline tune-up talk around that (ambiguous, claimed)

valve_covers.notes: very tight fit, valve cover puller tool supplied

oil_pressure_prime_psi.notes: on stand while priming; ~170 high side

service_intervals.run_counting: line-lock/burnout and knocking tires off at the line does not count as a run

power_claim.value: highest-horsepower engine the channel has had; 'more than you need' per Proline

failures.cause: George dropped a piston and rod on the floor; ~$5,000 joked cost
intentional small cosmetic scratch by crew (joke)

parts.notes: 'most expensive engine we've ever bought' - no price stated

parts.part: Set of connecting rods with correct bolts (service item)
parts.notes: caption garbled ('just under $22,000'), then clarified as two grand for a set; medium confidence
Proline: rods are cheap insurance vs ~$30k failure; one client failure cost ~19 rod sets

targets.notes: Get engine to Cameron Johnson Race Cars, install, race soon; track runs with Sharpie tally on car

cars.confidence: high for displacement/stroke/billet construction/torque specs; medium for rod price; low for firing order and limiter

reference_facts.fact: Proline moved to all-billet engines around 2011 after experience with a billet 41X-based engine
Anecdote: an aluminum 41 Hemi customer kept adding nitrous (75/125/150 shot) but only turned 8,200 rpm and survived - lower rpm extends life
Proline Hemis are common in Pro Mod; heads swapped every other round in Pro Mod
Early Hemi had reverse head studs into the valley requiring intake removal
Pulling heads on Mullet: ~75% of the work is removing the intake
Cleetus recently bought a Chrysler 300 (Hemi) for the $3,000 car challenge
